**Problem representation:** A man in his early forties with long-standing multiple sclerosis on ocrelizumab (10.6 years, 23 infusions) presents with a new respiratory illness five weeks after infusion, with hypogammaglobulinemia (IgG 422 mg/dL), HRCT ground-glass change with peripheral/migratory consolidation, and a lymphocyte-predominant BAL (69.7% lymphocytes), with SARS-CoV-2 excluded.

**Assessment:** The imaging pattern and marked BAL lymphocytosis are compatible with a hypersensitivity pneumonitis–like or drug-induced inflammatory lung reaction; ocrelizumab-associated ILD has been reported, and prolonged stable exposure does not exclude a late-onset immune-mediated complication. However, B-cell depletion plus IgG of 422 mg/dL substantially increases susceptibility to infections, including atypical bacterial, viral (non-SARS-CoV-2), fungal, and PJP, which can mimic ground-glass and consolidative change; BAL lymphocytosis alone does not exclude infection. Both inflammatory and infectious causes remain live hypotheses; neither is established by the supplied data.

**Still to be checked before causal attribution or treatment:** full microbiology (bacterial, mycobacterial, fungal, PJP, respiratory viral panels, aspirate/culture results), cryobiopsy or biopsy findings, serum IgM/IgA and specific antibody responses, comparison with prior imaging, temporal relationship to infusion and any other new drugs, and documented response to any treatment given. Only after excluding infection and confirming histologic inflammatory patterns should a drug-related attribution and decisions on ocrelizumab continuation be made.
